paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God had a plan from before the beginning, and it was always bigger than anybody guessed. The mystery is that through the gospel the Gentiles are "fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 3:6). If you came to God from the outside, you are not a guest at the end of the table. You are family, with the full share.

Now look at who God picked to carry this news. Paul, a prisoner, calls himself "less than the least of all the saints," and still says grace was given him to preach "the unsearchable riches of Christ" (Ephesians 3:8). I know a thing or two about being worn out and shoved in the back, so this hits me right in the apron. God doesn't need you to be impressive, baker. He gives the grace, and the grace does the work. And through the church, regular people like us, His wisdom gets shown off in the heavenly realms (Ephesians 3:10).

So here's what you take home. In Christ and through faith in Him, you can enter God's presence "with boldness and confidence" (Ephesians 3:12). No tiptoeing, no wondering if you belong. Paul even tells them not to be discouraged by his sufferings, because those sufferings are their glory (Ephesians 3:13). Walk in like you were invited, friend, because you were!
